question.text: Chapter 9 specifies that Category II AIFs can invest in SRs issued by ARCs because they are 'specifically categorised as __ under the SARFAESI Act for this purpose'. Fill the blank.

explanation.text: The Logic: Chapter 9: 'Category II AIFs can invest in SRs issued by ARCs as they are specifically categorised as Qualified Institutional Buyers under the SARFAESI Act for this purpose.' The QIB classification is what unlocks SR access for Cat II vehicles. The Trap: Option A (QB) is the SEBI ICDR definition — similar acronym, wrong regulation. Option C (AII) is invented. Option D (NBFC) is a separate corporate form, not an investor classification. Cross-Exam Context: XIX-A tests QIB status at distributor level. XV (Research Analyst) uses QIB in IPO-allocation contexts. III-A/C covers QIB under Issue of Capital Regulations. Manager's Pro-Tip: Maintain a QIB-status memo in the fund's compliance library — many Cat II AIFs assume QIB status automatically but the SARFAESI-specific classification is narrower than the SEBI ICDR QIB list. Document the legal opinion.
